shortDefinition: Re-running a fixed evaluation set after every change to catch outputs that used to be correct but have degraded.
fullDefinition: Regression testing for AI systems is the practice of treating outputs as behaviour that must not silently change. Because prompts, model versions, retrieval settings, and tool definitions all affect results, a change that improves one case frequently breaks another. A regression suite pins a versioned set of inputs, captures the expected qualities, and reruns the whole set on every change, flagging outputs that dropped below a threshold. Unlike conventional unit tests the outputs are not deterministic, so the suite needs tolerance: score thresholds, semantic similarity, or rubric-based judging rather than exact string comparison. The suite is most valuable when every production bug becomes a permanent case, so the same failure can never ship twice.
examples: Re-running the golden set whenever the system prompt is edited
Pinning a model version and testing before upgrading to the next
Turning every reported hallucination into a permanent test case
